title: Cleaning Up Orphaned RECURRENCE-ID Override Components When Series DTSTART or RRULE Moves

citations.verbatim_quote:
If present, this JSCalendar object represents one occurrence of a recurring JSCalendar object.  If present, the "recurrenceRules" and "recurrenceOverrides" properties MUST NOT be present.

   The value is a date-time either produced by the "recurrenceRules" of the base event or added as a key to the "recurrenceOverrides" property of the base event.

Purpose:  This property is used in conjunction with the "UID" and "SEQUENCE" properties to identify a specific instance of a recurring "VEVENT", "VTODO", or "VJOURNAL" calendar component.  The property value is the original value of the "DTSTART" property of the recurrence instance.

The entire event can be rescheduled using a "REQUEST".  This is done by using the "UID" of the event to reschedule and including the modified "RRULE".  Note that since this is an entire rescheduling of the event, any instance-specific information will be lost, unless explicitly included with the update "REQUEST".

rationale: By RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 and RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1, a recurrence override component's RECURRENCE-ID identifies the original DTSTART of a specific recurrence instance produced by the base component's recurrence rule. Meanwhile, RFC 5546 Section 4.4.7 notes that when rescheduling an entire event, instance-specific information is lost unless explicitly retained. When a whole-series edit (recurrence_id=None) modifies the master component's dtstart, rrule, or rdate, an existing override component's RECURRENCE-ID may no longer correspond to any occurrence of the updated master series (or, conversely, may still correspond to a valid occurrence if the new schedule still produces that timestamp). By store policy (synthesizing R-L4-003 override preservation with R-L4-004 EXDATE pruning), any override component whose RECURRENCE-ID is no longer generated by the master's updated (dtstart, rrule, rdate) MUST be removed from the calendar so orphaned exceptions do not linger, whereas any override component whose RECURRENCE-ID is still generated by the master's updated (dtstart, rrule, rdate) MUST be retained without overwriting the override's own dtstart/dtend/due with the master's new schedule.
store_implication: During a whole-series edit (recurrence_id=None) on a recurring series: after computing the updated master component (with new dtstart, rrule, rdate), the store MUST evaluate each existing override component (uid == target_uid, recurrence_id is not None, and neither rrule nor rdate is present) against the master component's candidate occurrence set (generated by (dtstart, rrule, rdate) before EXDATE subtraction). Override components whose recurrence_id timestamp (normalized to the master's timezone or DATE type) is NOT in the master's candidate occurrence set MUST be removed from the calendar (just as invalid EXDATEs on the master component are pruned per R-L4-004). Override components whose recurrence_id IS in the master's candidate occurrence set MUST be kept in the calendar, with only non-schedule metadata properties from the patch applied to the kept override (never overwriting the override's dtstart, dtend, due, or rrule with the master's schedule).
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Complete move past all overrides: A daily series at 2025-05-23 (COUNT=10) with an override at 20250527T090000 is moved to start on 2025-06-01. Because 2025-05-27T09:00:00 is no longer in the master series, the override component for 20250527T090000 must be removed whether the calendar was ordered [override, master] or [master, override].

Partial shift preserving overlapping override: A daily series at 2025-05-01T09:00:00 (COUNT=4) has two overrides: 20250501T090000 (moved to 10:00) and 20250503T090000 (moved to 11:00). The master series is shifted to start on 2025-05-02T09:00:00 (COUNT=3, covering May 2..4 at 09:00). The override for 20250501T090000 is no longer a valid occurrence and must be pruned, while the override for 20250503T090000 IS still a valid occurrence and must be preserved at 2025-05-03T11:00:00.

Time-of-day shift on master series: A daily series at 2025-05-01T09:00:00 (COUNT=5) with an override at RECURRENCE-ID 20250503T090000 is edited to start at 2025-05-01T14:00:00. Because the master occurrences are now at 14:00 instead of 09:00, 2025-05-03T09:00:00 is no longer in the master's recurrence set, so the 20250503T090000 override component is pruned.

Converting a recurring series to non-recurring (rrule=None and rdate=[]): All previously created RECURRENCE-ID override components sharing that UID are no longer valid recurrence instances of a recurring master and must be pruned along with master.exdate.

scenarios.name: move_series_partially_prunes_orphaned_override_and_keeps_valid_override
scenarios.description: Moving a daily series from May 1 (COUNT=4) with overrides on May 1 and May 3 to start on May 2 (COUNT=3, covering May 2, 3, 4) prunes the orphaned May 1 override while preserving the still-valid May 3 override.

audit_notes: Verified +/- 40 lines around all three citations (RFC 8984 Section 4.3.1 L1069-1075, RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 L6377-6381, and RFC 5546 Section 4.4.7 L5860-5864).

Reclassified authority from RFC_8984_CALEXT to STORE_POLICY: in RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5 (L1500-1502), a recurrenceOverrides key that does not match the recurrence rule is treated as an RDATE (additional occurrence), whereas in RFC 5546 Section 4.4.7 an entire reschedule drops all instance-specific overrides unless explicitly re-sent. Pruning overrides whose RECURRENCE-ID is no longer generated by the updated master's (dtstart, rrule, rdate) while retaining overrides whose RECURRENCE-ID remains valid is a store policy that keeps override retention (R-L4-003) and EXDATE pruning (R-L4-004) consistent.
Harmonized scenario and edge cases with R-L2-005 (exdate=[] on master alongside RECURRENCE-ID overrides) and unwrapped top-level JSON object.
